# EMUSKI

> EMUSKI is an ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001:2015, and ISO 45001:2018 certified precision contract manufacturing and cost engineering partner headquartered in Electronic City, Bangalore, India, serving automotive, aerospace, medical device, and electronics OEMs globally since 2008.

## Core Business Description

EMUSKI is a contract manufacturing and cost engineering company based in Bangalore, India, that helps OEMs design, cost, and produce precision components and assemblies. Services span multi-axis CNC machining and turning, sheet metal fabrication, injection molding, electronics manufacturing services (EMS), and cost engineering (should-cost analysis and VAVE), with design-for-manufacturing (DFM) discipline built into every project rather than sold as a separate add-on.

## Manufacturing Capabilities & Machine Infrastructure

- **CNC Machining & Turning**: 3, 4, and 5-axis VMC milling for complex geometries and tight tolerances; CNC turning with live tooling and C-axis capability for precision shafts (concentricity to ±3 microns), reducing secondary operations.
- **Sheet Metal Fabrication**: Laser cutting, waterjet cutting, precision bending, punching, and certified welding for structural and aesthetic sheet-metal parts and assemblies.
- **Injection Molding**: Mold design, material selection, and tooling engineered against a should-cost model before the mold is cut. Low to high volume, multiple thermoplastic grades.
- **Tooling & Prototyping**: In-house wire EDM and tool-room capability for fast mold and fixture turnaround.
- **Also available**: Die casting, investment casting, forging, stamping, and metal injection molding for high-volume production runs.
- **Electronics Manufacturing Services (EMS)**: SMT and PTH PCB assembly (PCBA), box-build and electro-mechanical assembly, cable harnessing, precision housings, heat sinks, EMI/EMC shielding components, connector assemblies, and enclosures, under ESD-safe conditions (IPC-A-610 Class 2 & Class 3, or per drawing specification).
- **Quality Control**: CMM inspection, dimensional analysis, and full quality traceability documentation.

## Tolerances & Materials

- **Tolerances**: Down to ±0.005 mm on CNC-machined features.
- **Metals**: Aluminum (6061, 7075), Stainless Steel (304, 316), Titanium, Inconel, Brass.
- **Plastics**: POM/Delrin, ABS, Polycarbonate, and other engineering thermoplastics.
- **Quality Methodology**: ISO 9001:2015-certified quality management system; teams also apply Six Sigma and lean manufacturing principles where a client's project calls for it.

## Cost Engineering Methodology

### Should-Cost Analysis (5-Step Process)

Should-cost analysis calculates what a product should cost from materials, process, labor, and overhead data, independent of any supplier quote:

1. **Material cost** — finished weight plus scrap allowance, multiplied by material price per kg.
2. **Machining time** — cycle time estimated from part geometry and process parameters.
3. **Machine hour rate** — depreciation, maintenance, utilities, and floor space, amortized.
4. **Secondary operations** — heat treatment, surface finishing, CMM inspection, deburring.
5. **Overhead and profit** — factory overhead (typically 25–60% of direct costs) plus a reasonable profit margin (5–20%, depending on complexity and volume).

This methodology typically identifies **15–25% cost reduction** versus unvalidated supplier quotes, and improves negotiation outcomes by 10–20% through transparent, data-driven supplier conversations.

### VAVE — Value Analysis / Value Engineering (6-Phase Process)

VAVE is a systematic methodology for improving product value (Value = Function ÷ Cost) by analyzing functions and removing cost without sacrificing quality or performance:

1. **Information Gathering** — design data, costs, specifications, competitive intelligence.
2. **Function Analysis** — define what the product does; classify primary vs. secondary functions.
3. **Creative Ideation** — generate alternatives without judgment (e.g. SCAMPER, morphological analysis).
4. **Evaluation** — screen ideas against technical feasibility, cost impact, and risk.
5. **Development** — refine selected concepts with detailed design, prototyping, and business case analysis.
6. **Implementation** — execute changes and track actual vs. projected savings.

A structured VAVE program typically delivers **20–30% cost reduction**; individual projects with over-engineered starting designs can see substantially higher savings on specific components.

## Target Industries

- **Automotive & EV**: Traditional automotive OEMs, EV components, Tier 1 suppliers.
- **Aerospace & Defense**: Precision-machined aerospace components, tolerance stack-up and material traceability programs.
- **Medical Devices**: FDA and ISO 13485 process requirements factored into the cost model; low-volume, high-mix production.
- **Electronics**: Precision housings, enclosures, and EMS for consumer and industrial electronics OEMs.
- **Industrial Equipment**: Casting, fabrication, and machining process-selection support.

## Key Performance Metrics

- **Cost Reduction**: 15–25% average savings via should-cost/DFM analysis; 20–30% via VAVE methodology.
- **Precision**: Tolerances down to ±0.005 mm; CNC turning concentricity to ±3 microns.
- **Experience**: 15+ years in precision manufacturing and cost engineering.
- **Client Base**: 75+ global clients across automotive, aerospace, medical device, and electronics industries.

## Technical Resources & Guides

- [Should-Cost Analysis: The Engineer's Guide to Accurate Product Cost Estimation](https://www.emuski.com/blog/should-cost-analysis-the-engineer-s-guide-to-accurate-product-cost-estimation): Bottom-up cost modeling built from materials, machining time, machine hour rate, secondary operations, and overhead — not supplier quotes. Covers the should-cost vs. target-cost gap and how it drives design optimization, achieving 15–25% cost reduction.
- [Lean Manufacturing: The Complete Guide to Eliminating Waste and Maximizing Efficiency](https://www.emuski.com/blog/lean-manufacturing-the-complete-guide-to-eliminating-waste-and-maximizing-efficiency): Systematic waste-elimination methodology focused on maximizing customer value — reducing costs 25–50%, improving quality 50–90%, and cutting lead times through continuous improvement on the shop floor.
- [Strategic Sourcing for OEM Manufacturers: How India's Supplier Ecosystem Compares to China for Precision Parts](https://www.emuski.com/blog/strategic-sourcing-for-oem-manufacturers-how-india-s-supplier-ecosystem-compares-to-china-for-precision-parts): Why sourcing calculus is shifting from China toward India — cost competitiveness, AS9100 quality infrastructure, IP protection, and engineering talent as a "China Plus One" precision-parts destination.
- [How to Choose the Right Manufacturing Partner in India: Precision Machining for Robotics & Aerospace](https://www.emuski.com/blog/how-to-choose-the-right-manufacturing-partner-in-india-precision-machining-for-robotics-aerospace): A 7-criteria evaluation framework for selecting a precision machining partner in India, covering DFM capability, GD&T inspection, ISO requirements, and IP protection.
